lines.text: Jess had waterproof boots, but every fall hike ended with wet socks.
Mud, wet leaves and little stones kept sliding in over the top.
They wrap from your laces up your shin, and cover the gap between boot and pants.
Rain, mud and debris slide off instead of falling in.
Jess hit the muddiest trail of the season, and came home with dry feet.
Save this before your next muddy hike.
